description: A real model's dashboard (deepseek-flash, the first live test): four cards in one column Stack with metrics, a progress bar, a horizontal bar chart, two tables and a callout. The terminal flows the cards into a grid and the metrics into a strip.

events.text:
Here's your disk usage:

```neoui
<Stack>
  <Card title="Disk /">
    <Header title="Disk usage" subtitle="/dev/nvme0n1p3 · mounted on / and /home"/>
    <Metric label="Used" value="820 GB" delta="of 896 GB" tone="danger"/>
    <Metric label="Free" value="72 GB" tone="success"/>
    <Progress value={0.92} label="92% used"/>
    <Text tone="muted">`/home/moritz` alone holds 756 GB of that.</Text>
  </Card>
  <Card title="Where the space goes (home)">
    <Header title="Top directories" subtitle="Home, GB"/>
    <BarChart labels={["Documents", ".cache", ".config", ".local", "Games", "Pictures", "vms", "Downloads", "Other"]} horizontal>
      <Series name="GB" values={[355, 65, 62, 60, 48, 25, 21, 17, 103]}/>
    </BarChart>
  </Card>
  <Card title="Documents breakdown">
    <Table columns={["Path", "Size", "Share of Documents"]} rows={[["neoworks", "210 GB", "59%"], ["clients", "45 GB", "13%"], ["playingwithclouds", "19 GB", "5%"], ["curseforge", "18 GB", "5%"], ["personal", "16 GB", "5%"], ["other (6+ dirs)", "47 GB", "13%"]]}/>
  </Card>
  <Card title="Cache — the cheap reclaim">
    <Header title=".cache" subtitle="65 GB total, mostly regenerable"/>
    <Table columns={["Cache", "Size", "Safe to delete"]} rows={[["uv", "18 GB", "Yes"], ["latent", "8.1 GB", "Probably"], ["go-build", "7.6 GB", "Yes"], ["ms-playwright", "3.2 GB", "Yes (re-download)"], ["huggingface", "3.2 GB", "Yes (re-download)"], ["spotify", "3.0 GB", "Yes"], ["yay", "2.9 GB", "Yes"], ["puppeteer", "2.0 GB", "Yes (re-download)"], ["zen", "1.9 GB", "Partly"], ["deno", "1.8 GB", "Yes"], ["rest", "13 GB", ""]]}/>
    <Callout tone="muted" title="Note">Deleting `.cache` content is safe — it's rebuilt on demand. Startup and first builds will be slower once.</Callout>
  </Card>
</Stack>
```
